title: Arcadia Insurance - POC scoping / workload modeling
summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on workload characterization for claims summarization and triage. Key asks: target QPS/concurrency, token distributions, latency SLOs, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and benchmark plan. Agreed next step: Redwood to run a 48-hour benchmark on Arcadia sample traffic and share latency/cost projections; customer to share sample logs and success criteria doc.
topics: Security and deployment options (VPC, KMS, SOC2)
Cost/throughput tradeoffs: hosted vs dedicated vs quantization
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-16 15:00 PST | Duration: ~52m | Recording: Fireflies export
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Noah Rivera (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Arcadia Head of ML), Rohit Verma (Platform), Diana Hale (Product), Evan Lee (Security)

[00:00] Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. this is Samira from Redwood, we have Liam and Noah with me, and I think we have the Arcadia crew - Maya, Rohit, Diana, Evan, is that right?
[00:06] Maya: yes hi, thanks for setting this up, excited to run through this.
[00:10] Liam: quick agenda: understand your success criteria, get the traffic profile (QPS, concurrency), token sizes and distributions, then we'll outline the benchmark plan and timeline.
[00:17] Rohit: sounds good. big picture: we want to pilot LLM-based claims triage and summarization. primary constraints are latency for the triage flow (~<300 ms p95 ideally) and cost - we do millions of requests monthly so unit cost matters.
[00:30] Noah: helpful - when you say millions monthly, do you have a rough QPS or concurrency number we should use for modeling?
[00:35] Maya: at peak we expect 1200 requests per minute for triage, so about 20 QPS. But there are bursts during morning/hourly rollups where concurrency could hit ~150 concurrent sessions for a short window. For summarization (longer outputs) it's lower QPS, maybe 5 QPS but big token outputs.
[00:52] Samira: ok good, so two main flows: triage (short input, short output, high QPS/bursty) and summarization (longer IO, lower QPS). can you share typical token counts?
[00:58] Diana: triage inputs are short, usually 80-120 tokens; outputs ~40-80 tokens. Summaries: inputs can be 1200-2500 tokens (full claim text + attachments parsed), outputs 200-500 tokens. We also have a reranker flow for suggestions with many candidates - that's chatty: 10-20 candidates per request, smaller outputs.
[01:18] Liam: great, that helps. to model cost and latency we need distribution - can you estimate percentiles? like 60% triage short, 30% summaries, 10% reranker?
[01:25] Maya: yes that's approximately right - triage is about 65%, summaries 25-30%, reranker 5-10.
[01:31] Rohit: one more infra note: we will be evaluating private deployment (VPC) vs Redwood dedicated. Security is essential - we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. Evan will own security review.
[01:45] Evan: yup also data residency - EU customers must stay in eu-west region. in POC we can keep data in us-west but need to validate cross-region requirements.
[01:54] Samira: understood - Redwood supports region pinning, VPC, and KMS/HSM integrations. we'll include security docs.
[02:00] Noah: digging into traffic modeling: with your peak 20 QPS triage and bursts to 150 concurrent, batching behavior matters. Redwood's runtime does adaptive batching; with small inputs we expect low batching efficiency but continuous batching can help. For p95 latency target ~300 ms, we'll need to measure tail behavior.
[02:18] Maya: can you run a benchmark with our spike patterns? we have synthetic traces we can share.
[02:22] Liam: yes - plan is: Arcadia shares 48 hours of anonymized sample request logs (timestamps + token counts + request types). Redwood will replay those against representative model variants and produce: QPS/concurrency over time, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, and cost estimates under hosted vs dedicated quantization profiles.
[02:39] Diana: timeline for that?
[02:40] Samira: we can start once we have the logs and a signed SOW/NDA if needed. initial benchmark results in 3-5 business days, extended 48-hour run and analysis 7-10 business days.
[02:52] Rohit: are you able to test quantized models? we have concerns about quality regressions.
[02:56] Liam: yes we test 8-bit/4-bit quant configs and measure quality with a small eval set from your prompts; we'll return BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics and qualitative failure cases. Redwood Optimize also suggests config tradeoffs - we can propose quantization profiles per workload.
[03:12] Maya: for success criteria - here's what we consider a win: p95 latency <=300 ms for triage at typical load (20 qps), p95 <=600 ms during burst windows up to concurrency ~150, summarization p95 <=2s, accuracy/on-topic rate >=95% for triage classification, and overall cost target under $0.00X per triage request (TBD).
[03:35] Noah: helpful. we'll model cost per request at different model sizes and quantization. Do you have preferred models or are you open to Redwood-curated open models?
[03:42] Maya: open to curated models as long as we can get deterministic latency. we have internal constraints preferring models with known license terms.
[03:49] Liam: noted. we'll pick 2 model variants: a smaller faster quantized model for triage and a larger model for summaries, plus a fallback mid-size model for resilience.
[03:58] Evan: on security during the benchmark - we need logs scrubbed, PII removed, and access limited. we'll also want to validate KMS integration before any production rollouts.
[04:08] Samira: understood - Redwood will provide scrubbing guidance and sample scripts, and we can run in a VPC test env if you prefer.
[04:15] Diana: operational question: what observability will we get for the POC?
[04:19] Noah: the Redwood Console gives per-route latency and token breakdowns, per-request traces (sampled), and rollout controls. we'll include a benchmark spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and token-per-request breakdowns.
[04:30] Rohit: what about concurrency spikes - does Redwood spin up nodes quickly?
[04:34] Liam: Dedicated pools can be configured with burst capacity; on hosted we rely on autoscaling which can take longer. for the POC we can provision dedicated capacity for short windows to simulate peak concurrency to get realistic tail latency.
[04:48] Maya: OK that seems fine. can you also include cost delta between keeping everything hosted vs dedicated reserved for the peak windows?
[04:55] Samira: yes cost modelling will include reserved dedicated commit scenarios vs hosted pay-as-you-go; we'll show per-token and per-request breakdowns.
[05:03] Diana: any immediate blockers from your side?
[05:06] Rohit: timeline - we need results before our Q2 infra planning meeting in three weeks.
[05:10] Samira: we can prioritize - if you share logs today we'll do an accelerated run and aim to deliver initial results in 4 business days.
[05:16] Noah: on the replay side we'll need the logs anonymized but keep timing fidelity, and a little metadata column for request type and candidate counts for reranker flow.
[05:25] Maya: noted, we'll send an S3 link with scrubbed logs and a short mapping doc of fields.
[05:30] Evan: also, share your SOC2 and data handling docs up front so security can triage.
[05:34] Samira: will attach Redwood security pack and provide the KMS integration doc.
[05:38] Liam: a few technical notes we discussed: 1) prefix/KV caching will help for repeated claims text patterns, 2) batching will be tuned - small inputs get limited batching benefits, 3) we'll measure GPU utilization to estimate cost efficiency.
[05:52] Rohit: for reranker flow with 10-20 candidates, do you recommend a two-stage approach? small model to filter then larger re-rank?
[05:58] Liam: yes that's common - a lightweight embed/filter stage then full rerank; it can reduce cost and latency. we'll include that architecture in the benchmark variants.
[06:07] Diana: great. lets recap next steps.
[06:10] Samira: recap: 1) Arcadia shares anonymized 48h logs + eval prompt set + SOW/NDA as needed; 2) Redwood runs benchmark: short smoke then 48h replay across model variants (quantized + baseline) and returns latency/cost/quality report; 3) Security docs shared by Redwood; 4) follow-up technical deep dive scheduled to review results and discuss Dedicated provisioning.
[06:33] Maya: agreed. target delivery: initial bench in 4 business days, full 48h analysis in 7-10 business days.
[06:40] Evan: I'll review security pack and get back with any gaps.
[06:44] Samira: ok thank you all. we'll send calendar invite for the technical follow-up.
[06:49] Meeting ends
next_steps: Arcadia to upload anonymized 48h request logs and sample eval prompts (S3 link)
Redwood to run accelerated benchmarks (3-5 business days for initial smoke, 7-10 days for full analysis)
Redwood to share security pack (SOC2, KMS integration docs, SAML/SSO notes)
Schedule technical deep dive to review benchmarks and Dedicated sizing
